<!-- Generated by go run ./internal/conn3x/provider/moddoc in conn3xorg/conn3x. Don't edit by hand. -->

A directory, created with its parents.

Use `directory` to make sure a directory exists on a host, with its mode and optionally its owner and group. Conn3x creates any missing parent directories too.

## Example usage

Create a directory:

```hcl
step "app_dir" {
  directory {
    path = "/opt/app"
  }
}
```

Set the owner, group and mode:

```hcl
step "app_data" {
  directory {
    path  = "/var/lib/app"
    owner = "app"
    group = "app"
    mode  = "0750"
  }
}
```

Create several directories, one instance per directory and host:

```hcl
step "app_tree" {
  for_each = ["/srv/app/releases", "/srv/app/shared", "/srv/app/logs"]
  directory {
    path = item.value
  }
}
```

Make sure an empty directory is gone, and stays gone:

```hcl
step "old_cache" {
  directory {
    path  = "/var/cache/app-legacy"
    state = "absent"
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | string | No | Owning group. Left as is when unset. |
| `mode` | string | No | Octal permissions. Defaults to "0755". |
| `on_remove` | string | No | "forget" (default) leaves the directory, "delete" removes it when it is empty. |
| `owner` | string | No | Owning user. Left as is when unset. |
| `path` | string | Yes | Absolute path. |
| `state` | string | No | "present" (default) or "absent", which removes the directory when it is empty and keeps it gone. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_directory.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | With state "absent", whether the directory is already gone. Null otherwise. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_directory` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Reading.** Every plan reads the directory on the host: whether it exists, its mode, and its owner and group. If something other than a directory is at the path, such as a file or a symbolic link, Conn3x stops with an error and doesn't replace it.

**Applying.** Conn3x runs `mkdir -p`, then sets the mode, owner and group. On SELinux hosts the directory is relabelled for its path with `restorecon`. Only the directory itself is changed. Missing parents are created by `mkdir -p` and aren't managed, and the directory's contents are left alone.

**Ownership.** `owner` and `group` are only checked and set when you give them. Leave them out and Conn3x keeps whatever the directory has.

**Mode.** The default mode is `"0755"`. If the mode on the host changes, the next plan shows the difference.

**Absent.** With `state = "absent"`, every plan checks only whether the directory exists. If it does, the plan shows the step out of sync and apply removes it. If it doesn't, the plan shows no change, and a directory that comes back later is removed again by the next apply. Only an empty directory is removed: one with anything in it is left in place, and the apply reports an error. `mode`, `owner` and `group` can't be set alongside it. A file, a symbolic link or anything else that isn't a directory at the path is an error, and is left in place.

A `directory` step acts as root on the path you name, and follows a symlink at that path. Don't manage a root-owned path inside a directory a non-root user can write to, because that user can swap what the path points to.

## Removal

When you delete a `directory` step, `on_remove` decides what happens on the host. The default, `"forget"`, leaves the directory where it is. `"delete"` removes it only when it's empty. A directory with anything in it is left in place, and the apply reports an error.

## From Ansible

`conn3x convert ansible` turns `file` tasks with `state: directory` into `directory` steps, with `mode`, `owner` and `group`. A task that sets `recurse` stays a TODO.
